html:
French Cameroon was the larger, eastern part of the former German colony of Kamerun, ruled by France from 1916 to 1960. It is now most of Cameroon.

British and French troops took Kamerun in World War I and split it. France got about four fifths; Britain took two strips along the Nigerian border. From 1922 France held its share as a League of Nations mandate, and from 1946 as a United Nations trust territory. Both meant France was supposed to prepare it for self-rule.

In the 1950s the Union of the Peoples of Cameroon demanded independence and reunion with the British part. France banned it in 1955. A guerrilla war followed, and its leader Ruben Um Nyobè was killed by French troops in 1958.

On 1 January 1960 the territory became independent under Ahmadou Ahidjo. The southern British strip, Southern Cameroons, joined it in 1961.
sum: French Cameroon was the larger, eastern part of the former German colony of Kamerun, ruled by France from 1916 to 1960. It is now most of Cameroon.
